## claude.ai Dropbox
# Claude App MCP LLM Boot Instructions

You are the assistant for Dropbox's Claude App MCP server. Your goal is to help users complete Dropbox tasks quickly and correctly while minimizing friction.

## Customer Use Cases

This app is best at helping users do these Dropbox workflows:

- Browse folder contents and paginate through large directories.
- Find files quickly using plain-language search terms and then open files with follow-on tools.
- Inspect file metadata (size, type, timestamps, IDs, sharing context).
- Check signed-in Dropbox identity, team/account context, and namespace-root context.
- Read text content from supported files up to 5 MiB, and provide a usable Dropbox link even when text extraction fails.
- Generate single-use temporary download links when the user explicitly needs direct file download URLs.
- Generate file previews with thumbnail and "open in Dropbox" experiences.
- Create folders in the right destination before saving artifacts.
- Create new text files directly in Dropbox.
- Create share links for files/folders and return the effective sharing settings.
- Inspect and list existing shared links.
- List, inspect, and create Dropbox file requests.
- Move, rename, copy, and delete Dropbox files/folders after explicit confirmation.
- Check the status of long-running move, copy, and delete jobs.

When users ask "what can you do?", summarize these use cases in plain language before taking action.

## Not Supported (Do Not Advertise)

- Editing or overwriting existing file content in place.
- Saving URL-hosted files directly into Dropbox.
- Uploading local/binary artifacts via `upload_file`.
- Permanent file deletion or wipe workflows. `delete` moves items to the user's Dropbox "Deleted files" area only.
- Reliable text extraction for supported files via `fetch`; extraction may still fail for some files, in which case the tool error may include a usable link.
- E-signature initiation or signing workflows.
- Actions outside Dropbox content management and sharing.

## devonthink
CRITICAL — Database package safety: DEVONthink databases are stored as packages (.dtBase2) or sparse images (.dtSparse, .dtArchive). Never modify, rename, move, or delete files inside a database package directly via the filesystem. All record and content operations must go through this MCP server or, as a fallback, via AppleScript. Direct filesystem manipulation will corrupt the database and cause irreversible data loss.

Batch operations: Use the uuids array parameter instead of sequential single-record calls for tag, update, move, trash, duplicate, replicate, and export operations. Batch mode is faster, reduces round trips, and returns a summary with succeeded/failed counts.

Avoiding duplicates: Use lookup_records (by name, URL, path, filename, or comment) before create_record to check whether a record already exists.

Content editing: Prefer update_record_content with mode append or insert over replace for large documents. Replace mode requires sending the entire new content and risks accidental data loss if the content is incomplete.

Group hierarchies: Use create_group_path to create nested group structures in a single call (like mkdir -p) rather than sequential create_record calls.

AI-powered tools: classify_record and find_similar_records use DEVONthink's built-in AI algorithms and proprietary training data — they provide organizational suggestions that complement, not duplicate, your own capabilities.

Record enrichment: resolve_doi_metadata and resolve_book_metadata can enrich existing records with bibliographic metadata by passing the record's uuid — there is no need to create a new record.

AI exclusion: Records marked as excluded from AI access (excludeFromChat) are protected in two ways. (1) Input protection: any tool that receives such a record's UUID as an argument refuses to operate on it and returns an error. (2) Output protection: result lists from tools like search_records, classify_record, find_similar_records, get_record_children, get_record_duplicates, and the link traversal tools are filt… [truncated]

## omnifocus
OmniFocus is a GTD task manager. Hierarchy: Folders > Projects > Tasks > Subtasks.

TASK STATES: Available, Blocked, Deferred (future defer date), Flagged, Overdue, Completed, Dropped. Planned Date is a scheduling signal only — no availability/overdue constraints.

PROJECT TYPES: "sequential" (tasks in order; first incomplete = available, rest blocked; position = dependencies), "parallel" (all available), "single_actions" (no completion goal, cannot auto-complete). The `next` field is true for the first available action in a sequential project/action group; in parallel projects, all incomplete tasks have `next: true`.

ACTION GROUPS: Task with subtasks. Parent shows `blocked: true` while subtasks are active — this is normal, not an error. Do not try to unblock it.

INHERITED STATUS: `completed`/`dropped` reflect the task's own state, not its container's. `effectivelyCompleted`/`effectivelyDropped` reflect the container's state — if true, the task's parent project or action group was completed/dropped. Task in completed project: `completed: false`, `effectivelyCompleted: true`, `available: false`. Use `available_only=True` for actionable tasks.

EFFECTIVE DATES: Dates returned by get_tasks are always effective (inherited). A task with no direct due date WILL show its project's due date in the dueDate field — this is correct behavior, not a bug. You cannot clear an inherited date at the task level. Write operations set the task's own date.

RECURRING TASKS: `completed=True` uses `mark complete`, which creates the next occurrence. This is guaranteed. WARNING: Dropping a recurring task (status='dropped') without clearing recurrence first (recurrence='') spawns the next occurrence. To stop a series: update_tasks([{"id": "...", "recurrence": "", "status": "dropped"}]).

TAGS: Represent work contexts. Tag statuses: Active (normal), On Hold (tasks excluded from Available perspective), Dropped (tag hidden from picker; does NOT affect task availability).

DEFER vs DUE: Defer = hidden until that date. Due = deadline.

1	# Classify / Reclassify on the Receipts Page — Design
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-08-03
4	**Status:** ✅ Built (pending release) — Category column on Receipts, `CategoryDropdown`
5	repositioned with `@floating-ui/dom`, vendor rules applied by an AFTER INSERT trigger,
6	`autoAssignCategoryBestEffort` deleted, sweep added to the Receipts page. The
7	[deferred RPC move](#deferred-finish-the-migration-and-delete-the-typescript-normalizer)
8	is still deferred, and the [split-receipt question](#out-of-scope) is still open.
9	
10	You can classify an expense on the Expenses page. On the Receipts page you can
11	only do it by opening a receipt's edit modal — where the dropdown is clipped out
12	of view, which is the logged bug _"Category dropdown clipped"_. So in practice
13	the Receipts page cannot classify anything.
14	
15	Fixing that turned out to be two changes, not one. The visible half is a Category
16	column on the receipts table plus a dropdown that stops being clipped. The
17	invisible half is larger and more valuable: **vendor rules move from the client to
18	the database**, so a receipt is categorized when it is created rather than when
19	someone happens to visit the right page.
20	
21	## What exists today
22	
23	The Expenses page has the full feature — a `category` column marked
24	`interactive: true` so clicking it does not open the receipt modal
25	(`src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte:1236`, `DataTable.svelte:179`), rendering
26	`CategoryDropdown` with search, keyboard navigation, inline category creation and
27	a vendor-rule panel. `handleCategorySelect` (`:282`) persists immediately,
28	auto-creates a vendor rule, applies it to other visible rows, toasts, and fans out
29	to a multi-row selection via `applyCategoryToSelection` (`:208`).
30	
31	The Receipts page has none of it. Its table is Image / Date / Merchant / Amount /
32	Actions (`src/routes/receipts/+page.svelte:908`) — no Category column, so you
33	cannot see which receipts are uncategorized, let alone change one. The only path
34	is the edit modal, and `ReceiptEditModal` wraps its body in `overflow-y-auto p-6`
35	(`:234`), which is exactly the clipping trap CLAUDE.md documents: a container
36	whose overflow is non-visible in one axis clips absolutely-positioned children in
37	_both_.
38	
39	`handleCategoryChange` on the receipts page (`:263`) has also drifted from its
40	Expenses twin — it assigns and creates a rule, but never applies the rule to other
41	rows and shows no feedback at all.
42	
43	### The domain-model tension, and why we are crossing it
44	
45	[The domain model](../domain-model.md) says: _"Talk about Expenses when reporting
46	or categorizing; talk about Receipts when capturing."_ This design puts
47	categorizing on the capture surface.
48	
49	That line was already crossed by the edit modal (`#{#rmc2a}`), so the column is a
50	consistency fix rather than a new boundary violation. The workflow argument is the
51	real one: you upload a batch of receipts, you are looking at them, and the app
52	sends you to a different page to say what they are. The glossary entry should be
53	amended when this lands rather than left contradicting the UI.
54	
55	## Changes
56	
57	### 1. Category column on the receipts table
58	
59	Between Amount and Actions, `interactive: true`, rendering the existing
60	`CategoryDropdown` — the same arrangement as Expenses.
61	
62	Behaviour is **identical to the Expenses column**, via one extracted
63	implementation rather than a third copy of the same logic:
64	
65	- persists immediately on pick, no Save;
66	- auto-creates a vendor rule for that merchant when none exists;
67	- applies that new rule to other visible uncategorized rows;
68	- toasts the count;
69	- picking a category on a row that is part of a multi-row selection sets the
70	  whole selection.
71	
72	Two supporting edits. `applyRuleToVisibleExpenses` (`ExpenseService.ts:414`)
73	currently takes `Expense[]`, but the receipts page holds `ReceiptRow[]` plus a
74	separate `categoryMap`; it only reads `receipt_id`, `merchant_name` and
75	`category_id`, so its parameter type widens to those three fields. And the
76	receipts page already owns `receiptSelection`, so the fan-out costs almost
77	nothing.
78	
79	**No sort on the column and no Uncategorized filter.** The Receipts FilterPanel
80	already carries six controls and the uncategorized queue belongs on Expenses.
81	
82	### 2. The dropdown stops being clipped
83	
84	`@floating-ui/dom` is promoted to a direct dependency. It is already resolved in
85	the lockfile as a dependency of `flowbite-svelte@1.33.1` (which we use for
86	`Datepicker`), so this adds no new supply-chain surface and `min-release-age` is
87	not a factor.
88	
89	`CategoryDropdown`'s menu (`CategoryDropdown.svelte:375`) swaps
90	`absolute right-0` for a fixed, floating-ui-positioned element with `flip`,
91	`shift` and `autoUpdate`. Markup, `data-testid`s and the existing spec suite stay
92	intact — this is a positioning change to one `<div>`.
93	
94	One fix closes three bugs:
95	
96	| Where                                                           | Clipping container                                              |
97	| --------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
98	| Receipt edit modal — the logged bug                             | `ReceiptEditModal.svelte:234`, `overflow-y-auto p-6`            |
99	| The new Receipts column, on phones                              | `DataTable.svelte:108`, `overflow-x-auto … sm:overflow-visible` |
100	| The Expenses column, on phones — **broken in production today** | same line                                                       |
101	
102	Rebuilding `CategoryDropdown` on flowbite-svelte's own `Dropdown` was considered
103	and rejected: it wraps the same library but would restructure a component
104	carrying search, keyboard nav, inline creation and the vendor-rule panel, for the
105	same outcome.
106	
107	### 3. Vendor rules are applied by the database, not the client
108	
109	Today rule application lives in `ReceiptService.autoAssignCategoryBestEffort`
110	(`:417`), called from `uploadAndCreate` (`:259`) after OCR. It
111	covers exactly one of the ways a receipt can come into existence:
112	
113	| Creation path                                                      | Rules applied today?                                         |
114	| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
115	| `uploadAndCreate` (`ReceiptService.ts:237`)                        | ✅                                                           |
116	| `createManual` (`:166`)                                            | ❌                                                           |
117	| `splitReceipt` (`:494`)                                            | ❌                                                           |
118	| `ExpenseImportService.insertReceipts` (`:217`)                     | n/a — category comes from the import file, `source='manual'` |
119	| Email → `resend/handler.ts:165`, via `insert_receipt_with_context` | ❌                                                           |
120	
121	**Replace it with a trigger on `receipts` AFTER INSERT** that looks up
122	`vendor_category_rules` by family + normalized merchant and inserts
123	`expense_categories` with `source='auto'` **only when no row exists**.
124	`merchant_name` is present on the row at insert time in every path
125	(`buildReceiptInsert` at `:257` fills it from the OCR extract before `:258`
126	inserts), so the trigger always has what it needs.
127	
128	`autoAssignCategoryBestEffort` is then **deleted**, not left alongside. Two
129	implementations of one rule is the failure mode this change exists to remove.
130	
131	This closes the existing backlog item _"Email-flow vendor auto-assignment (the
132	email path never applies the vendor rule)"_ as a side effect, and covers any
133	creation path added later without anyone remembering to wire it up.
134	
135	The alternative — extend the client helper to `createManual` and `splitReceipt`,
136	then write a second implementation in Deno for the email path — was rejected
137	because it creates a second instance of the pain CLAUDE.md already warns about
138	for `supabase/functions/_shared/` date-correction code having to stay in lock-step
139	with `src/lib/utils/`.
140	
141	### 4. The page-load sweep stays, and now runs on Receipts too
142	
143	`applyAllVendorRules` runs on Expenses page load
144	(`expenses/+page.svelte:144`). With a trigger categorizing at creation it looks
145	redundant, but it is not: when a rule is created, `handleCategorySelect` applies
146	it to **`filteredExpenses`** (`:313`), not to every expense. Receipts outside the
147	current filter, or on another family member's screen, stay uncategorized, and the
148	load sweep is the only thing that ever catches them.
149	
150	It therefore stays as the retroactive net, and is added to the Receipts page —
151	otherwise the new column would show stale "Uncategorized" rows that silently fix
152	themselves the moment you visit Expenses.
153	
154	Making rule creation apply to _all_ expenses and deleting the sweep entirely is
155	the cleaner end state, but "I categorized one Starbucks and it rewrote 400
156	receipts" needs its own confirmation UX. Not in this change.
157	
158	### 5. What does not change
159	
160	The edit modal keeps its deferred Save/Cancel contract for category
161	(`ReceiptEditModal.svelte:59`, `:76`, `:143`). The rule is coherent as stated:
162	_inside a Save/Cancel modal everything defers; direct manipulation in the table is
163	immediate._ Making category alone instant inside the modal would break Cancel for
164	that one field and drop it out of the unsaved-changes guard.
165	
166	## Testing
167	
168	Trigger coverage goes in the integration suite, alongside
169	`src/lib/tests/family-category-visibility.spec.ts` — which is already the working
170	precedent: it drives `vendor_category_rules` and `expense_categories` against a
171	live local Postgres, creates and tears down its own families and users per
172	`beforeEach`, and guards itself with
173	`describeIf(Boolean(URL && SERVICE_KEY))`. It even declares `testReceiptId` with
174	the comment _"No test creates a receipt yet; cleanup guards on it"_ — the receipt
175	cleanup path is already wired for exactly this.
176	
177	Run with `npm run test:integration` (which injects the local stack's URL and
178	service-role key via `local:env`), and `npm run db:reset` before pushing the
179	migration.
180	
181	**Accepted downgrade, stated plainly.** `ReceiptService.autoCategory.spec.ts` is
182	a 15-case pure-mock suite that runs inside the build gate today
183	(`vercel.json` → `vitest run --project server`) and genuinely blocks a deploy.
184	Its replacement cannot: Vercel's build image has no Postgres, so the integration
185	spec sits inside the gated run but self-skips there, and
186	[ADR-0005](../adr/0005-quality-gate-in-the-vercel-build-not-github-actions.md)
187	deliberately keeps GitHub Actions out of the release path. Trigger tests will be
188	run on demand, locally. This was a deliberate choice over two alternatives that
189	were offered and declined: a shared normalizer fixture keeping half the check
190	inside the gate, and running the integration suite in the advisory workflow.
191	
192	That is a workable position **only because the person who runs the tests and the
193	person who ships are the same person**. It stops being workable the moment a
194	second contributor arrives, and it is not a judgement that the gap does not
195	matter — the wider "stack-dependent suites run nowhere automatically" problem is
196	tracked separately in the backlog and deserves its own decision, on the merits of
197	the RLS suite rather than this feature.
198	
199	**One thing to do anyway, because it is nearly free.**
200	`ExpenseService.vendorRules.spec.ts:170` already has a
201	`'Vendor name normalization'` case list. Assert the SQL `normalize_vendor()`
202	against **that same list** in the integration suite. It gates nothing, but it
203	means whoever edits one implementation gets a red test from the other the next
204	time they run integration — and the backlog item asking `normalizeVendor` to start
205	dropping trailing store numbers makes that edit a near-certainty rather than a
206	hypothetical.
207	
208	## Risks
209	
210	**Normalizer parity — the sharp one.** `vendor_pattern` is stored
211	already-normalized by `createVendorRule`, so the trigger only normalizes the
212	incoming merchant name. That SQL `normalize_vendor(text)` must match
213	`ExpenseService.normalizeVendor` (`:321`) character for character —
214	`lower()`, strip everything outside `[a-z0-9\s]`, collapse whitespace. A mismatch
215	raises no error anywhere; rules simply stop matching, silently, and the symptom is
216	"auto-categorization quietly stopped working" weeks later. With the testing
217	decision above there is no gated check on this. Make the SQL function the single
218	canonical definition, and test it directly in the integration suite against the
219	same cases `ExpenseService` uses.
220	
221	This risk exists because the design deliberately stops halfway — see
222	[the deferred RPC move](#deferred-finish-the-migration-and-delete-the-typescript-normalizer),
223	which removes the risk class rather than mitigating it.
224	
225	**Bulk import fires the trigger per row.** `ExpenseImportService.insertReceipts`
226	(`:217`) inserts in chunks _before_ `insertExpenseCategories` writes the file's
227	own categories. Correctness is fine — the file's `source='manual'` upsert wins on
228	conflict, and rows the file left blank now get rule-categorized, which is an
229	improvement. But a thousands-row historical import now performs a rule lookup per
230	inserted row. Measure it against a realistic import before shipping.
231	
232	**The trigger is invisible.** A future reader debugging "why did this receipt get
233	a category" has no client-side code to step through. The migration needs a comment

# Classify / Reclassify on the Receipts Page — Design

**Date:** 2026-08-03
**Status:** ✅ Built (pending release) — Category column on Receipts, `CategoryDropdown`
repositioned with `@floating-ui/dom`, vendor rules applied by an AFTER INSERT trigger,
`autoAssignCategoryBestEffort` deleted, sweep added to the Receipts page. The
[deferred RPC move](#deferred-finish-the-migration-and-delete-the-typescript-normalizer)
is still deferred, and the [split-receipt question](#out-of-scope) is still open.

You can classify an expense on the Expenses page. On the Receipts page you can
only do it by opening a receipt's edit modal — where the dropdown is clipped out
of view, which is the logged bug _"Category dropdown clipped"_. So in practice
the Receipts page cannot classify anything.

Fixing that turned out to be two changes, not one. The visible half is a Category
column on the receipts table plus a dropdown that stops being clipped. The
invisible half is larger and more valuable: **vendor rules move from the client to
the database**, so a receipt is categorized when it is created rather than when
someone happens to visit the right page.

## What exists today

The Expenses page has the full feature — a `category` column marked
`interactive: true` so clicking it does not open the receipt modal
(`src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte:1236`, `DataTable.svelte:179`), rendering
`CategoryDropdown` with search, keyboard navigation, inline category creation and
a vendor-rule panel. `handleCategorySelect` (`:282`) persists immediately,
auto-creates a vendor rule, applies it to other visible rows, toasts, and fans out
to a multi-row selection via `applyCategoryToSelection` (`:208`).

The Receipts page has none of it. Its table is Image / Date / Merchant / Amount /
Actions (`src/routes/receipts/+page.svelte:908`) — no Category column, so you
cannot see which receipts are uncategorized, let alone change one. The only path
is the edit modal, and `ReceiptEditModal` wraps its body in `overflow-y-auto p-6`
(`:234`), which is exactly the clipping trap CLAUDE.md documents: a container
whose overflow is non-visible in one axis clips absolutely-positioned children in
_both_.

`handleCategoryChange` on the receipts page (`:263`) has also drifted from its
Expenses twin — it assigns and creates a rule, but never applies the rule to other
rows and shows no feedback at all.

### The domain-model tension, and why we are crossing it

[The domain model](../domain-model.md) says: _"Talk about Expenses when reporting
or categorizing; talk about Receipts when capturing."_ This design puts
categorizing on the capture surface.

That line was already crossed by the edit modal (`#{#rmc2a}`), so the column is a
consistency fix rather than a new boundary violation. The workflow argument is the
real one: you upload a batch of receipts, you are looking at them, and the app
sends you to a different page to say what they are. The glossary entry should be
amended when this lands rather than left contradicting the UI.

## Changes

### 1. Category column on the receipts table

Between Amount and Actions, `interactive: true`, rendering the existing
`CategoryDropdown` — the same arrangement as Expenses.

Behaviour is **identical to the Expenses column**, via one extracted
implementation rather than a third copy of the same logic:

- persists immediately on pick, no Save;
- auto-creates a vendor rule for that merchant when none exists;
- applies that new rule to other visible uncategorized rows;
- toasts the count;
- picking a category on a row that is part of a multi-row selection sets the
  whole selection.

Two supporting edits. `applyRuleToVisibleExpenses` (`ExpenseService.ts:414`)
currently takes `Expense[]`, but the receipts page holds `ReceiptRow[]` plus a
separate `categoryMap`; it only reads `receipt_id`, `merchant_name` and
`category_id`, so its parameter type widens to those three fields. And the
receipts page already owns `receiptSelection`, so the fan-out costs almost
nothing.

**No sort on the column and no Uncategorized filter.** The Receipts FilterPanel
already carries six controls and the uncategorized queue belongs on Expenses.

### 2. The dropdown stops being clipped

`@floating-ui/dom` is promoted to a direct dependency. It is already resolved in
the lockfile as a dependency of `flowbite-svelte@1.33.1` (which we use for
`Datepicker`), so this adds no new supply-chain surface and `min-release-age` is
not a factor.

`CategoryDropdown`'s menu (`CategoryDropdown.svelte:375`) swaps
`absolute right-0` for a fixed, floating-ui-positioned element with `flip`,
`shift` and `autoUpdate`. Markup, `data-testid`s and the existing spec suite stay
intact — this is a positioning change to one `<div>`.

One fix closes three bugs:

| Where                                                           | Clipping container                                              |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Receipt edit modal — the logged bug                             | `ReceiptEditModal.svelte:234`, `overflow-y-auto p-6`            |
| The new Receipts column, on phones                              | `DataTable.svelte:108`, `overflow-x-auto … sm:overflow-visible` |
| The Expenses column, on phones — **broken in production today** | same line                                                       |

Rebuilding `CategoryDropdown` on flowbite-svelte's own `Dropdown` was considered
and rejected: it wraps the same library but would restructure a component
carrying search, keyboard nav, inline creation and the vendor-rule panel, for the
same outcome.

### 3. Vendor rules are applied by the database, not the client

Today rule application lives in `ReceiptService.autoAssignCategoryBestEffort`
(`:417`), called from `uploadAndCreate` (`:259`) after OCR. It
covers exactly one of the ways a receipt can come into existence:

| Creation path                                                      | Rules applied today?                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `uploadAndCreate` (`ReceiptService.ts:237`)                        | ✅                                                           |
| `createManual` (`:166`)                                            | ❌                                                           |
| `splitReceipt` (`:494`)                                            | ❌                                                           |
| `ExpenseImportService.insertReceipts` (`:217`)                     | n/a — category comes from the import file, `source='manual'` |
| Email → `resend/handler.ts:165`, via `insert_receipt_with_context` | ❌                                                           |

**Replace it with a trigger on `receipts` AFTER INSERT** that looks up
`vendor_category_rules` by family + normalized merchant and inserts
`expense_categories` with `source='auto'` **only when no row exists**.
`merchant_name` is present on the row at insert time in every path
(`buildReceiptInsert` at `:257` fills it from the OCR extract before `:258`
inserts), so the trigger always has what it needs.

`autoAssignCategoryBestEffort` is then **deleted**, not left alongside. Two
implementations of one rule is the failure mode this change exists to remove.

This closes the existing backlog item _"Email-flow vendor auto-assignment (the
email path never applies the vendor rule)"_ as a side effect, and covers any
creation path added later without anyone remembering to wire it up.

The alternative — extend the client helper to `createManual` and `splitReceipt`,
then write a second implementation in Deno for the email path — was rejected
because it creates a second instance of the pain CLAUDE.md already warns about
for `supabase/functions/_shared/` date-correction code having to stay in lock-step
with `src/lib/utils/`.

### 4. The page-load sweep stays, and now runs on Receipts too

`applyAllVendorRules` runs on Expenses page load
(`expenses/+page.svelte:144`). With a trigger categorizing at creation it looks
redundant, but it is not: when a rule is created, `handleCategorySelect` applies
it to **`filteredExpenses`** (`:313`), not to every expense. Receipts outside the
current filter, or on another family member's screen, stay uncategorized, and the
load sweep is the only thing that ever catches them.

It therefore stays as the retroactive net, and is added to the Receipts page —
otherwise the new column would show stale "Uncategorized" rows that silently fix
themselves the moment you visit Expenses.

Making rule creation apply to _all_ expenses and deleting the sweep entirely is
the cleaner end state, but "I categorized one Starbucks and it rewrote 400
receipts" needs its own confirmation UX. Not in this change.

### 5. What does not change

The edit modal keeps its deferred Save/Cancel contract for category
(`ReceiptEditModal.svelte:59`, `:76`, `:143`). The rule is coherent as stated:
_inside a Save/Cancel modal everything defers; direct manipulation in the table is
immediate._ Making category alone instant inside the modal would break Cancel for
that one field and drop it out of the unsaved-changes guard.

## Testing

Trigger coverage goes in the integration suite, alongside
`src/lib/tests/family-category-visibility.spec.ts` — which is already the working
precedent: it drives `vendor_category_rules` and `expense_categories` against a
live local Postgres, creates and tears down its own families and users per
`beforeEach`, and guards itself with
`describeIf(Boolean(URL && SERVICE_KEY))`. It even declares `testReceiptId` with
the comment _"No test creates a receipt yet; cleanup guards on it"_ — the receipt
cleanup path is already wired for exactly this.

Run with `npm run test:integration` (which injects the local stack's URL and
service-role key via `local:env`), and `npm run db:reset` before pushing the
migration.

**Accepted downgrade, stated plainly.** `ReceiptService.autoCategory.spec.ts` is
a 15-case pure-mock suite that runs inside the build gate today
(`vercel.json` → `vitest run --project server`) and genuinely blocks a deploy.
Its replacement cannot: Vercel's build image has no Postgres, so the integration
spec sits inside the gated run but self-skips there, and
[ADR-0005](../adr/0005-quality-gate-in-the-vercel-build-not-github-actions.md)
deliberately keeps GitHub Actions out of the release path. Trigger tests will be
run on demand, locally. This was a deliberate choice over two alternatives that
were offered and declined: a shared normalizer fixture keeping half the check
inside the gate, and running the integration suite in the advisory workflow.

That is a workable position **only because the person who runs the tests and the
person who ships are the same person**. It stops being workable the moment a
second contributor arrives, and it is not a judgement that the gap does not
matter — the wider "stack-dependent suites run nowhere automatically" problem is
tracked separately in the backlog and deserves its own decision, on the merits of
the RLS suite rather than this feature.

**One thing to do anyway, because it is nearly free.**
`ExpenseService.vendorRules.spec.ts:170` already has a
`'Vendor name normalization'` case list. Assert the SQL `normalize_vendor()`
against **that same list** in the integration suite. It gates nothing, but it
means whoever edits one implementation gets a red test from the other the next
time they run integration — and the backlog item asking `normalizeVendor` to start
dropping trailing store numbers makes that edit a near-certainty rather than a
hypothetical.

## Risks

**Normalizer parity — the sharp one.** `vendor_pattern` is stored
already-normalized by `createVendorRule`, so the trigger only normalizes the
incoming merchant name. That SQL `normalize_vendor(text)` must match
`ExpenseService.normalizeVendor` (`:321`) character for character —
`lower()`, strip everything outside `[a-z0-9\s]`, collapse whitespace. A mismatch
raises no error anywhere; rules simply stop matching, silently, and the symptom is
"auto-categorization quietly stopped working" weeks later. With the testing
decision above there is no gated check on this. Make the SQL function the single
canonical definition, and test it directly in the integration suite against the
same cases `ExpenseService` uses.

This risk exists because the design deliberately stops halfway — see
[the deferred RPC move](#deferred-finish-the-migration-and-delete-the-typescript-normalizer),
which removes the risk class rather than mitigating it.

**Bulk import fires the trigger per row.** `ExpenseImportService.insertReceipts`
(`:217`) inserts in chunks _before_ `insertExpenseCategories` writes the file's
own categories. Correctness is fine — the file's `source='manual'` upsert wins on
conflict, and rows the file left blank now get rule-categorized, which is an
improvement. But a thousands-row historical import now performs a rule lookup per
inserted row. Measure it against a realistic import before shipping.

**The trigger is invisible.** A future reader debugging "why did this receipt get
a category" has no client-side code to step through. The migration needs a comment
saying what it does and why the client helper was deleted.

## Deferred: finish the migration and delete the TypeScript normalizer

This design leaves the vendor-rule engine **split across two languages**: the
trigger matches in SQL, the retroactive application matches in TypeScript. That
seam is what the normalizer-parity risk above is. It can be closed, and the
option is recorded here so the half-migration is a known state rather than an
accident someone stumbles on later.

Every caller of `normalizeVendor` is vendor-rule plumbing inside
`ExpenseService`; none of it needs to be client-side for any UI reason:

```
normalizeVendor                     ExpenseService.ts:321
  ├─ getVendorRule                             :346   ← read, for the dropdown's rule panel
  ├─ createVendorRule                          :385   ← normalizes before insert
  ├─ applyRuleToVisibleExpenses                :432   ← matching
  └─ expenses/+page.svelte              :311, :377    ← only compute an argument for the above
```

Move those four into RPCs and the TypeScript normalizer has no callers left and
is deleted. One definition of vendor identity, no parity to maintain, nothing for
a future CI system to have to catch. It would also collapse `applyAllVendorRules`
— which today loops rules client-side with a round-trip each — into a single
statement.

Note this is **not** the rejected "apply to all expenses instead of
`filteredExpenses`" change from §4. An RPC taking `(family_id, merchant_name,
category_id, receipt_ids[])` normalizes in SQL while preserving the visible-only
scope exactly as it is today.

**Why it is deferred rather than done now.**
`ExpenseService.vendorRules.spec.ts` holds **38 mock-based cases** — rule
lookup, creation, normalization, family isolation, preserve-existing-
categorizations, large-dataset performance, edge cases — all of which currently
run inside the build gate. Moving the logic to SQL moves all 38 out of it, on top
of the 15 from `autoCategory.spec.ts`. That would put the entire vendor-rule
feature beyond machine verification in one step, at a moment when the only thing
watching is a human remembering to run `npm run test:integration`.

The trade is worth making **after** the stack-dependent-suites question in the
backlog is answered, not before. The trigger earns its place in this change
because it fixes real broken behaviour — three creation paths that never apply
rules, including email ingestion. The RPC move fixes no user-visible defect; it
buys design purity at the cost of 53 gated tests. Different justification,
different timing.

## Out of scope

**Split receipts.** What a Split Receipt should inherit is a real question — the
merchant's rule, or the parent's current category, which may have been manually
reclassified away from that rule — and it needs more work than this change should
absorb. Punted deliberately. **Note the consequence:** the trigger will apply the
merchant rule to splits by default, because `splitReceipt` copies the original's
merchant into a new row. That is an unexamined default, not a decision. Logged in
the backlog.

## Sequencing

1. `@floating-ui/dom` as a direct dependency; reposition `CategoryDropdown`'s
   menu. Independently shippable — it fixes the logged modal bug and the
   already-broken Expenses column on phones without touching anything else.
2. Extract the shared category-assignment logic from
   `expenses/+page.svelte:282`, add the Category column to the receipts table,
   widen `applyRuleToVisibleExpenses`.
3. Migration: `normalize_vendor(text)` + the AFTER INSERT trigger. Verify with
   `npm run db:reset`.
4. Delete `autoAssignCategoryBestEffort` and `ReceiptService.autoCategory.spec.ts`;
   port the cases into the integration suite, and assert `normalize_vendor()`
   against the existing case list at `ExpenseService.vendorRules.spec.ts:170`.
5. Add the `applyAllVendorRules` sweep to the Receipts page.
6. Amend the [domain model](../domain-model.md) glossary line about categorizing
   belonging to Expenses.

# Receipt Notes — Design

**Date:** 2026-08-03
**Status:** ✅ **Done** — all eight sequencing steps landed 2026-08-03 (pending
release). `receipts.notes` + CHECK, the `Note (optional)` textarea with counter and
save-gating, previews on both list pages, splits copying the note, and
`buildReceiptPatch` replacing the three page-level patch literals. The two live bugs
this design uncovered (§5 and the `original_filename` half of §6) were fixed first,
ahead of the feature.

**One verification step was still outstanding when this closed:** `npm run db:reset`
has **not** been run against the migration — Docker was unavailable on both attempts.
CLAUDE.md requires it before pushing, so it is tracked in the
[backlog](../product-backlog.md) rather than here, where nobody would look for it.

Decisions below were settled in a grilling session on 2026-08-03; deferred items are
listed under [Deferred](#deferred).

A Receipt records merchant, amount and date, and nothing else a person can say in
their own words. Everything else the app knows is either extracted from the image
or inferred. So there is nowhere to write down _"Sam's birthday gift"_,
_"reimbursable — client dinner"_, or _"warranty runs to 2028"_ — the reasons a
purchase actually mattered.

This adds one free-text field to the Receipt, editable in the receipt edit modal,
with a truncated preview on the Receipts and Expenses lists.

It is a small feature that landed on top of a real bug. Adding a column to
`receipts` means touching **five hand-maintained field lists**, none of which the
compiler checks — and one of the five was a synthetic `ReceiptRow` on the Expenses
page that had been **silently destroying data in production**. Designing notes is
what surfaced it, so it was fixed first; see §5.

## What exists today

`receipts` has no note-like column (`supabase/migrations/20260726120000_baseline.sql:595`)
and nothing in `Receipt.ts` is close. `ReceiptEditModal` (shared by the Receipts,
Expenses and Reconciliation pages) edits nine fields; both list pages render an
explicit `DataTable` `columns` array (`receipts/+page.svelte:908`,
`expenses/+page.svelte:1220`).

| #   | Location                                                    | Silent failure if `notes` is omitted                                      |

| 1   | `ReceiptService.#EDITABLE_FIELDS` (`ReceiptService.ts:118`) | `update()` strips the field. No error, no save.                           |
| 2   | patch literal, Receipts page (`+page.svelte:218`)           | Note never saves from Receipts                                            |
| 3   | patch literal, Reconciliation page (`+page.svelte:384`)     | Note never saves from Reconciliation                                      |
| 4   | patch literal, Expenses page (`+page.svelte:555`)           | Note never saves from Expenses                                            |
| 5   | `isDirty` in the modal (`ReceiptEditModal.svelte:68`)       | Closing with an unsaved note gives **no warning** — the note is discarded |

All five are inferred object literals or a string `Set`, so omitting a field
type-checks cleanly. They have already drifted: the Receipts patch carries
`suspicious_date` (`:228`) and the Reconciliation patch does not (`:392`).
